BASE.name: ATTACK_VECTOR
BASE.justification: Secrets embedded in Visualforce or Lightning files can be accessed remotely through web applications or exposed front-end code.

BASE.name: ATTACK_COMPLEXITY
BASE.justification: Once the secret is exposed in client-side or easily accessible files, exploitation is straightforward.

BASE.name: PRIVILEGES_REQUIRED
BASE.justification: An attacker does not require privileges if the secret is exposed in publicly accessible pages or resources.

BASE.name: USER_INTERACTION
BASE.justification: No user interaction is required once the attacker obtains the exposed secret.

BASE.name: SCOPE
BASE.justification: Exposed secrets in frontend code can impact external systems or services beyond the original application boundary.

BASE.name: CONFIDENTIALITY
BASE.justification: Hardcoded secrets such as API keys or tokens can grant unauthorized access to sensitive data and backend systems.

BASE.name: INTEGRITY
BASE.justification: Compromised secrets may allow attackers to modify data or perform actions as trusted users or systems.

BASE.name: AVAILABILITY
BASE.justification: Misuse of exposed secrets may disrupt services or exhaust resources, though availability is not the primary impact.

TEMPORAL.name: EXPLOIT_CODE_MATURITY
TEMPORAL.justification: Exploitation of exposed secrets is well known and easily reproducible using common techniques.

TEMPORAL.name: REMEDIATION_LEVEL
TEMPORAL.justification: The recommended fix is to remove secrets from code and use secure storage such as protected configuration or secret management systems.

TEMPORAL.name: REPORT_CONFIDENCE
TEMPORAL.justification: The issue is reliably detected by GitLeaks and maps to a well-known CWE for hardcoded credentials.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_ATTACK_VECTOR
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: In deployment, exposed secrets remain accessible through network-facing web applications.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_ATTACK_COMPLEXITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Environmental conditions do not increase the difficulty of exploiting exposed secrets.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_PRIVILEGES_REQUIRED
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Possession of the exposed secret is sufficient to exploit the issue.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_USER_INTERACTION
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: No additional user interaction is required in the deployed environment.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_SCOPE
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Secrets may allow access to external systems, extending impact beyond the original application boundary.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_CONFIDENTIALITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Exposed secrets in production can lead to unauthorized access to sensitive user data, APIs, or external services.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_INTEGRITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Attackers may perform unauthorized actions or alter data using compromised credentials.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_AVAILABILITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Availability may be affected through abuse of access, but this is not the primary risk.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: CONFIDENTIALITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Protecting secrets in frontend code is critical as they can expose access to sensitive systems and data.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: INTEGRITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Maintaining trust in system operations and preventing misuse of exposed credentials is critical.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: AVAILABILITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Availability is important as misuse of secrets may disrupt services, though confidentiality and integrity are higher priorities.
